description: Complete Phase 1 Task 1.3 (AST integration). The doc claims ast.rs is a stub, but tree-sitter parsing, find_node_at, and get_context already work. The genuine functional gap is get_containing_function, which always returns None because AstNode has no parent tracking and find_function_in_hierarchy never walks upward. Fix get_containing_function so it correctly returns the name of the function/method enclosing a given SourceLocation, for all supported grammars (python, javascript, rust, c, cpp). Add tests that would fail against the current broken behaviour. This is independent of the Python-binding features (FEAT-002/003) and touches only xplainit-core.
steps: In xplainit-core/src/ast.rs, implement get_containing_function so it actually finds the innermost enclosing function/method for a location. Recommended approach: walk the tree-sitter tree directly (the Tree is retained in self.tree) rather than the parent-less AstNode copy - descend to the node at the location, then walk up node.parent() until a node whose kind contains 'function' or 'method' (grammar-appropriate: e.g. Python 'function_definition', JS 'function_declaration'/'method_definition', Rust 'function_item', C/C++ 'function_definition') is found, then read its 'name'/'declarator' field. If staying with AstNode, add parent tracking (e.g. store the containing-function name during convert_node, or record parent indices) so the upward search works.

Ensure the fix works across languages: verify Python, JavaScript, and Rust at minimum by parsing a small snippet with a named function and asserting get_containing_function for a location inside the body returns the function name.

Add #[cfg(test)] unit tests in ast.rs: (a) parse Python 'def foo():\n    x = 1' and assert get_containing_function for the line of 'x = 1' returns Some("foo"); (b) a JavaScript function case; (c) a Rust fn case; (d) a location outside any function returns None. These tests must fail against the current implementation (which returns None) and pass after the fix.

If practical without adding dependencies or destabilizing the API, surface AST-derived function context in the ast_parsing example (xplainit-core/examples/ast_parsing.rs) so get_containing_function is demonstrated; keep it optional if it risks breaking the example.
Run `cargo test -p xplainit-core` and confirm the new AST tests pass and existing ast tests still pass.
Run `cargo run --release --example ast_parsing -p xplainit-core` and confirm it still runs successfully.
acceptance_criteria: get_containing_function returns Some(function_name) for a location inside a function body (verified for Python, JavaScript, and Rust) and None for a location outside any function.
New ast.rs unit tests pass and would fail against the pre-fix implementation.
`cargo test -p xplainit-core` all green; existing ast_parsing example still runs.
findings: Rewrote get_containing_function in xplainit-core/src/ast.rs to walk the retained tree-sitter Tree directly (self.tree) instead of the parent-less AstNode copy. New helpers: smallest_node_at (descends to the innermost node whose line range contains the location), is_function_node (matches function-like kinds per grammar: Python function_definition; JS function_declaration/function/function_expression/method_definition/arrow_function/generator variants; Rust function_item; C/C++ function_definition), function_name (reads the 'name' field, falls back to descending the 'declarator' field for C/C++ via name_from_declarator). The upward walk SKIPS anonymous function nodes (no resolvable name, e.g. JS arrow functions) and continues to the nearest NAMED enclosing function, so a line inside a JS callback resolves to the outer named function. Added 6 #[cfg(test)] tests in ast.rs: python (foo), javascript (bar), javascript method (greet), rust (baz), c (add), and outside-any-function returns None. All would have returned None pre-fix and now pass. Also surfaced get_containing_function in examples/ast_parsing.rs for Python/JS/Rust. NOTE on line indexing: SourceLocation.line is 0-based (tree-sitter row); tests/example use 0-based lines accordingly. Verification: `cargo test -p xplainit-core` => 82 unit (76 baseline + 6 new) + 9 integration + 1 doctest all pass; `cargo clippy -p xplainit-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0; `cargo run --release --example ast_parsing -p xplainit-core` runs and prints calculate_total / processOrder / fibonacci for the sampled locations. No new dependencies added. Did NOT run cargo fmt --all per orchestrator guidance (repo not fmt-clean at baseline); matched local style in edited files.
